title: La Trobada
description: The flavor of coming together has a Mediterranean taste. A 52 m² neighborhood bar in Casagemes, Badalona.

blocks.title: La Trobada
blocks.subtitle: The flavor of coming together has a Mediterranean taste.

children.text: La Trobada is a neighborhood bar run by a Catalan-Valencian couple, proudly embracing Mediterranean essence and tradition in both hospitality and gastronomy.
We undertook a comprehensive redesign—including the graphic identity designed by sens*hac—to align the business identity with a warm atmosphere and agile operations between the bar and dining room.

images.alt: La Trobada menu and graphic identity
Mediterranean ceramic latticework by Ceràmica Ferrés

children.text: The opening of Hospital Quirón just a few meters from the restaurant triggered the project, aiming to attract new walk-in customers, streamline operations, and increase the average check.

items.alt: Overview of the dining room and bar at La Trobada
Interior view of the entrance and high tables at La Trobada

children.text: In terms of visual identity, the starting values were deeply rooted in Mediterranean culture. The space needed to convey the character and warmth of the coast through a natural color palette and materials drawn from local tradition, such as ceramics, lime plaster, and Catalan terracotta tiles. Honest, simple, and comfortable furniture completes this identity.

blocks.alt: Mediterranean material palette and furniture board for La Trobada

children.text: 1. Bogart high stools by Vergès / 2. Clay mortar wall finish / 3. Traditional terracotta tile by Ferres / 4. Wall sconce by Marset / 5. Tableware by Aguadé Cerámica / 6. Ceramic latticework element by Ferres.

The main goal was to resolve circulation between the kitchen, the dining room, and the terrace, which quadruples the indoor capacity. Avoiding cross-traffic between workflows—food service, coffee preparation, payments, and clearing—was essential to improving team operations.

To achieve this, we modified the street-facing enclosure and created an independent service station combining coffee preparation, clearing, and the beverage fridge, strategically positioned next to the dining-room entrance to speed up service.

items.alt: Independent service station between terrace and dining room
Undulating ceramic latticework above the bar at La Trobada

children.text: Yet the most distinctive and evocative element of the project is undoubtedly the large ceramic latticework above the bar. Its sinuous curve evokes the movement of the sea and becomes the space's most recognizable gesture—a form that transcends interior design and carries over into the menu design, adopting its undulating geometry as a visual thread.

blocks.alt: Reorganized bar, kitchen, and high-table seating area

children.text: We reorganized the kitchen, moving hot food prep to the wall opposite the bar and placing cold prep behind the bar, opening up space for bar seating. We also reoriented the furniture and replaced low tables with high tables to encourage turnover and reactivate an underused interior dining room.

To complete the intervention, we built a large custom storage cabinet in the corridor between the dining room and restrooms to house dining and terrace supplies, including cutlery, condiment baskets, preserves, and beverage stock.
